title: Trace integrity through a distributed CDN
description: Switch scenarios to see whether asset bytes and the expected digest retain independent paths. Select any component to inspect its responsibility during delivery and recovery.

nodes.label: Release publisher
nodes.detail: Creates immutable bytes, computes their digest, and authorizes one release identity. Its signing authority must remain separate from CDN delivery credentials.

nodes.label: Immutable origin
nodes.detail: Stores versioned objects without overwriting an existing key. Operators compare these bytes with the build artifact during an incident.

nodes.label: Release record
nodes.detail: Binds the asset URL, algorithm, digest, and release ID in authenticated HTML or a signed manifest.

nodes.label: CDN edge A
nodes.detail: Caches one immutable object near the user. A bad disk, stale fill, or compromised credential can make this edge disagree with the origin.

nodes.label: CDN edge B
nodes.detail: Provides another delivery route only when its bytes are independently verified against the same trusted release record.

nodes.label: Browser verifier
nodes.detail: Computes the digest, compares it with the authenticated SRI value, and prevents a mismatched script or stylesheet from loading.

nodes.label: Integrity telemetry
nodes.detail: Groups failures by release, asset, edge, and time window so responders can distinguish one poisoned cache from a broad rollout fault.

scenarios.label: Healthy release
scenarios.summary: Edge A returns the immutable release bytes while authenticated HTML supplies the independently protected digest.
scenarios.result: The computed digest matches the trusted release record, so the browser executes the asset and records a successful verification.

scenarios.label: Poisoned edge
scenarios.summary: Edge A returns changed bytes under the release URL, but it cannot rewrite the digest carried by authenticated HTML.
scenarios.result: The browser detects the mismatch and blocks execution. Responders preserve the edge response, compare it with origin bytes, and quarantine or purge the affected object.

scenarios.label: Verified failover
scenarios.summary: Traffic moves away from the affected edge, but the alternate copy must still match the same independently trusted release digest.
scenarios.result: Edge B is a safe fallback because its bytes verify before execution. Routing to another location without repeating verification would only move the trust assumption.

scenarios.label: Coupled metadata
scenarios.summary: A compromised edge returns malicious bytes and a matching digest sidecar through the same authority. No independent release path reaches the verifier.
scenarios.result: The hash comparison passes but publisher authenticity is lost. Move the expected value into authenticated HTML or a signed manifest controlled outside CDN write authority.
